title: Day 5 of my stock bot competition - Strategy 9 is +$1,578.70 (+31.57%)
author: DadsGamesandCharles
selftext:
Quick recap for anyone new: over the past year I've built a bunch of AI trading bots, and on Oct 22 I started a public paper-money competition with 13 accounts at $5,000 each (10 strategies, an account that follows Charles 2.0, which is a prediction engine that posts its up-picks the day before, an AI agent's account called Brokgot, and my own hand-traded account). This is the day 5 update, covering everything through the Oct 28 close. If you read my last post (day 4, the one with the rough Tuesday), you can skip straight to the results.

https://i.redd.it/g4a0acgygbyh1.png

https://i.redd.it/onxob5e2hbyh1.png

Everything below is paper money. Nobody steps in to fix the accounts.

**SPY for comparison**

SPY, close to close: Oct 22 -1.18%, Oct 23 -0.52%, Oct 26 +0.71%, Oct 27 +0.56%, Oct 28 +0.34%. From the Oct 21 close to the Oct 28 close, SPY is down about 0.10%. Over the same stretch the 10 strategies combined are up 6.97% in paper dollars, and all 13 accounts together are up 5.11%.

That's five sessions. It still means very little, and one trade in particular did a lot of the work today (more on that below).

**Today, Oct 28: a big day for Strategy 9**

The 10 strategies combined made $1,039.53 today while SPY rose 0.34%. Most of that was one account. Strategy 9 made $855.92, almost all of it from a single UPB trade: it bought shortly after the open and sold around 11:30 AM for a realized +$855.93. I'm genuinely excited about it, and Strategy 9 is now up 31.57% since the start. But I want to be straight about what it is. One trade made more than half of that account's total gain, so this is a very small sample, and I'm not going to pretend one great trade proves a strategy. It was already the leader before today, though (up about 14.5% at yesterday's close), so I'm watching to see whether it keeps that up on ordinary days too.

The rest of the strategies had small, steady green days: Strategy 8 +$36.30, Strategy 10 +$26.96, Strategy 2 +$20.03, Strategy 1 +$21.77, Strategy 4 +$21.02, Strategy 6 +$18.51, Strategy 5 +$15.81, Strategy 3 +$14.42, Strategy 7 +$8.79. All ten strategies finished the day green.

INTC dipped right after it got in, so the timing just didn't work out. Brokgot sat today out entirely and just stayed in cash. After a rough Tuesday, that's a legitimate choice, and its balance stayed at $4,622.69.

**The part where I get a lesson in self-control: SNAP**

My hand-traded account is holding SNAP, and it's down, so here's the honest story.

Position facts at the Oct 28 close: about 3,908 shares, average entry $6.22 (bought Oct 27 around 9:41 AM), official close $5.96, which is an unrealized paper loss of about $1,016. The stock itself is down about 4.2% from my entry, and for the account it's a much bigger percentage, because this is the whole account in one position. It lost $468.99 today and the account total is now +$60.69 (+1.21%), down from +$530 yesterday and +$980 at the Oct 26 close. I'm marking it at the Oct 28 official close of $5.96 in the table above.

Why am I holding it? Earnings. I normally don't enter a trade before earnings, not even a scalp, but I like SNAP, so I did it anyway. Per Snap's own announcement, the Q3 2026 earnings call is Wednesday, Nov 4 at 5:00 PM ET, so after the market closes.

And here's the lesson part. The best moment this trade ever had was right after I bought it. Going back through the minute-by-minute data, SNAP touched about $6.24 around 9:41 AM, about two cents above my entry. The stock was only up about 0.3% at that point, but on my position that was roughly $79 on paper, which was about 1.3% of the account. That was the peak, not a gain I locked in, and I did not sell. It was never anywhere near a big win. Then it dipped, and I said, no worries, it's SNAP, it'll go back up. And it did, back up to the mid-$6.10s on Tuesday, still under my entry but the right direction. At that point I decided it was building momentum and I didn't want to sell a recovery in the middle. Then it went down again on Wednesday and has stayed down. Taking about $79 wouldn't have been exciting, but it would have beaten where I am now. I turned a small green moment into a big red one. Stocks go up and down, and I think it eventually goes back up. It's SNAP, so probably not too long.

I'm pretty confident about the direction. I can't tell you when. All of this account's money is tied up in this one trade, and I don't want to hurt my win rate or my ROI on the account. I also know that the longer I hold it, the more risk I take on, and I'm still going to hold it. That's me being stubborn, and I'm calling it that.

My own opinion and plan, not a prediction and definitely not advice: I figure Thursday is when it makes the move I want, and judging by how it traded today, I think Friday morning will be decent, with a lot of selling after that. I could be wrong about every part of this. This is paper money, and I'm showing it as a lesson in how easy it is to talk yourself out of a plan. It is not a recommendation to buy, hold or sell anything.

**How Charles 2.0's picks did today**

The four picks were set the evening before. For each one I checked whether the stock's high for the day, between the 9:30 AM open and 3:59 PM, reached +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0% above the 9:30 AM open, using minute bars. A touch just means the price reached that level at some point. It doesn't mean anyone could have sold there.

1. INTC: high +0.63% above the open. Touched +0.25% and +0.5%, not +1.0%.
2. UPB: high +7.55% above the open. Touched all three levels.
3. FROG: high +1.72% above the open. Touched all three levels.
4. CLF: high +1.16% above the open. Touched all three levels.

So four of four touched +0.25%, four of four touched +0.5%, and three of four touched +1.0%.

Running tally for live Charles 2.0 picks, Sep 22 through Oct 28 (27 sessions, 108 picks): 95 touched +0.25% above the open (88%), 86 touched +0.5% (80%), and 69 touched +1.0% (64%). What I care about is whether a pick reaches those levels during the day, since I want the money that same day, not the next. But I'm not going to oversell it: a touch is not the same as a profit someone could capture. You'd have to be out at or near the high, and nobody knows the high in advance.

A note on the tally: I recomputed every pick since Sep 22 from full minute data after noticing gaps in what I had stored for some days. That nudged one number from my last post: the +1.0% touch count goes from 64 to 66 as of Oct 27 (the +0.5% count stays at 82). The numbers above use the recomputed data.

**What I'm not claiming**

The live touch rates are decent, but a touch is not a profit. The price reaching a level at some point in the day doesn't mean anyone could have sold there. I haven't shown that these picks beat random ones. Calling any of this proven would be wrong, so I'm not. Strategy 9's day is one trade, and my own SNAP position is a reminder that I'm not a perfect trader either. Some people have had doubts about the strategies, and that's fair. The competition is how we find out in public.

**What would prove me wrong**

If the combined bots trail SPY over a meaningful stretch, or if live touch rates drift toward what random picks would get, then the story I'm telling is wrong and I'll say so here.

**What's next**

Daily results from now on, and a fuller write-up as the sample grows. I'll also update you on the SNAP position either way, good or bad.

**Questions you probably have**

Is this real money? No. Every account is paper money.

Is paper trading realistic? Not entirely. Paper can't show market impact, and real fills are usually worse. That's the main reason my early backtests got cut down.

Will you ever trade real money? Yes, we will.

Can I buy or subscribe to anything? Not yet.

Is this financial advice? No. The picks are research ideas to watch, not tips, and nothing here is a guarantee of anything. My SNAP trade is an example of a hand trade and a lesson, not a recommendation.

Are AI agents involved? Yes. AI agents help build, test and run the bots, and one of the accounts is traded by an AI agent. I'm the one who reviews and posts this.

Why don't you share the rules? Because the strategies are the project. I'll share the results, the accuracy and the picks before they play out.

Why publish bad numbers? Because a track record that only shows the good days isn't worth much.

What if a bot loses? Then it loses in public. The accounts are paper and no one steps in to fix them.

Why did the competition start on Oct 22? Earlier starts on Monday and Tuesday had account setup problems, so those days don't count.

Where can I follow along? On this profile. I'll post daily results here after the close.

Have a question that isn't here? Ask in the comments and I'll answer it.

*Paper money only. Not financial advice. Written with help from AI.*

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good that you say plainly that one trade drove most of the best account's gain and that a touch isn't a profit. Since you haven't shown the picks beat random ones, the cleanest check is to run the same touch test on random stocks on the same days and compare the rates. With 13 accounts running at once, a few will lead by luck, so I'd judge them by how they do after the day they were picked as the leader. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is built for this kind of check, with a fee setting and a held out stretch of data.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
The thing about the way Charles picks his stocks is that a lot of them historically rise about 4% on the day so one big gain on one day is kind of normal for Charles also.

The main thing that I wanna know is if the accounts run for two weeks, which one ends up being the most profitable per day. Once I figure that out, don’t know how to tweak it even more

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That makes sense, and a big day being normal for those picks is useful to know. The catch with picking the winner after two weeks is that with this many accounts, one will usually lead by luck. The better test is to see if the leader stays ahead over the next two weeks, because that's when luck fades out.

each account is a different strategy

and no, not the exact rules, sorry, that's the part I've put a ton of time into. The general idea is that each morning my model ranks stocks it thinks have the best shot at a quick move up that day. The bots take its top picks, try to grab part of the early move, and are usually out the same day. The 10 strategies all start from the same picks but handle getting in and out differently, which is why their results spread out so much
